memory_candidates.content: When committing to a JSON file (e.g. index-entries.json) that is shared across concurrently-dispatched sibling tasks in a batch /orchestrate run, a plain `git add <path>` stages the ENTIRE working-tree version of that file, sweeping in any sibling's uncommitted-but-live edits (e.g. line_count fixes from their own generate-context-line-counts.sh --write run) and misattributing them to your commit. Isolate your commit instead: (1) capture git show HEAD:<path> as the clean base, (2) apply only your own structural change to that base via jq (not to the dirty working-tree copy), (3) temporarily write that clean result to the working-tree file, (4) run the normal scoped-commit script against it, (5) immediately restore the original dirty working-tree content (your change + sibling's pending edits) afterward so the sibling's in-flight work remains present and uncommitted for their own later commit. This keeps commits attributionally clean without reverting or blocking any sibling's concurrent progress.

When splitting one markdown file into several (command-body slimming / mode extraction), grep for positional cross-references ('above', 'below', 'this section', 'the following') that assumed single-file adjacency BEFORE assuming a bare grep for the other section's NAME catches every broken reference. A reference like 'following the same fallback used by Sync Mode below' survives a 'grep for other mode names' sweep (it does name the mode) but becomes false once Sync Mode is relocated to its own file and is no longer literally 'below'. Fix by replacing the positional word with an explicit pointer to the now-separate file (e.g. 'Sync Mode (context/patterns/task-sync-mode.md)'), not just by confirming the mode name itself still appears.

For a verbatim markdown section-relocation task, a byte-ledger reconciliation (bytes removed from the source file must equal bytes relocated to new files minus/plus the measured pointer-text delta, with the residual computed exactly rather than estimated) is a strong, cheap proof that nothing was lost or duplicated during extraction. Measuring each piece (old bullet bytes vs new pointer bytes, old region bytes via a captured temp file) and summing to confirm a 0 B residual catches content loss that a mere 'file still parses' check would miss.
